notes_excerpt: DESCRIPTION: Bank deposit and loan interest ratesNOTES:n.p.: non publishable for reasons of confidentiality.Notes (for interest rates up to June 2010):(1) The calculation of the average interest rates does not include consignations (special type of deposit liabilities with a zero interest rate).(2) The average interest rates (I, Ia, Ib, II, IIa, IIb, III) are calculated using as weights the outstanding volumes of deposits - loans.The evolution of these average rates depends both on the level of the individual interest rates and on the market shares of each type of deposit-loan.To mitigate the effect of abrupt changes in market shares, the calculation of the weighted average rate is based on the 12-month moving average market shares.(3) The loans to sole proprietors are included in loans to non-financial corporationsNotes (for interest rates from June 2010):(1) The calculation of the average interest rates does not include consignations (special type of deposit liabilities with a zero interest rate).(2) The average interest rates (I, Ia, Ib, II, IIa, IIb, IIc, III) are calculated using as weights the outstanding volumes of deposits - loans.The evolution of these average rates depends both on the level of the individual interest rates and on the market shares of each type of deposit-loan.To mitigate the effect of abrupt changes in market shares, the calculation of the weighted average rate is based on the 12-month moving average market shares.(3) The loans to sole proprietors are not included in loans to non-financial corporations.(4) Debit balances on current accounts of sole proprietors are included in the debit balances on current accounts of individuals and individual non-profit institutions.(5) According to the Bank of Greece Governor’s Act 2672/5.5.2014, debt restructuring operations below market conditions are not included in the compilation of the average interest rates on new business, as of June 2014.DISCLAIMER: The data sets are provided for statistical use and research purposes. notes_excerpt: DESCRIPTION: MFI credit to the Greek economyΝΟΤΕS: Amounts at end of period in million euros, including securitized loans serviced by credit institutions as well as debt securities.As of June 2010 loans to sole proprietors are no longer included in loans to corporations but as a separate subcategory of loans. Moreover loans to private non-profit institutions include loans to religious institutions.Loans to public corporations that have been reclassified (in accordance with a decision by ELSTAT in November of 2010) from the private to the public sector are included in credit to general government as of Dec 2009.As of June 2010 non traded corporate bonds are included in 'loans' rather than 'debt securities'.In August 2011 domestic credit institutions registered a reduction in the value of their portfolio of Greek Government securities amounting to EUR 4 billion because of their participation in the securities exchange programme agreed by the EU Summit of 21st July 2011. In January 2012 credit institutions registered a further reduction in the value of this portfolio amounting to EUR 5.8 billion, in March 2012 a reduction of EUR 15.2 billion and in April 2012 a reduction of EUR 4.1 billion.As of December 2016, loans of the Consignment Deposits and Loan Fund are excluded from the domestic credit as the institution has been reclassified from the financial sector to the general government sector.ADVANCE RELEASE CALENDAR: MFI credit to the Greek economyDISCLAIMER: The data sets are provided for statistical use and research purposes. They are subject to revisions according to a well-defined revision policy in order to improve their quality. The latest version of each data set replaces all previous ones. The user is responsible for taking into account the most recent metadata and all supplementary information that accompanies each data set before using it.

notes_excerpt: DESCRIPTION: External debtΝΟΤΕS:Note 1: Amounts in million of euros, end of reporting period - in market value. Gross External Debt Data will be announced no later than 90 days after the end of the reference period.Note 2: Gross External Debt includes only liabilities vis-a-vis foreign countries of all institutional sectors-both private and public-of the Greek economy, such as Monetary Authorities (i.e the Bank of Greece), Other Monetary Financial Institutions, General Government and Other Sectors (including non-monetary financial institutions and non-financial enterprises). A more detailed view of external assets and liabilities of these sectors is available under International Investment Position dataset of Greece.Note 3: Short term Currency and Deposits of Central Bank comprises liabilities to Eurosystem related to TARGET.Note 4: In relation with General Government Gross External Debt in Securities, the first and second quarter of 2012, the Greek government bond exchange programme was completed under the PSI. The new bonds issued following the PSI are marked to market. However, bonds held by the ECB and the Eurosystem NCBs (SMP+ANFA) are not marked to market, but instead are marked at face value. In the fourth quarter of 2012, the Greek government buyback programme was completed. The acceptance of offers to exchange designated securities had a positive effect on Public Debt; However this is not accounted for EXD since the reporting data is given at market values.Note 5: Other debt liabilities comprise insurance, pension, and standardized guarantee schemes, and other accounts payable–other in the international investment position (IIP) statement.Note 6: Concerning category Loans of Other Sectors it also includes loans transferred to foreign financial corporations and whose servicing has been assigned to domestic Credit Servicing Firms operating according to Law 4354/2015.ADVANCE RELEASE CALENDAR: Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS) / 2.External sector / 2.1.Advance release calendarMETADATA: External debtNamely, for Gross External Debt: https://www.bankofgreece.gr/RelatedDocuments/SDDS-BOG-SITE-METADATA-CONTACT_PERSONS-EXD.pdfDISCLAIMER: The data sets are provided for statistical use and research purposes. notes_excerpt: DESCRIPTION: Bulletin of conjunctural indicatorsNOTES: The nominal effective exchange rate (NEER) is the weighted geometric mean of the price of a representative basket of foreign currencies, with each currency weighted on the basis of its importance in the country's external trade. The broad NEER index compiled by the Bank of Greece comprises Greece's bilateral exchange rates vis-à-vis its 28 major trading partners within and outside the euro area, and weights are calculated on the basis of Greece's imports and exports of manufacturing goods (categories 5-8 of the Standard International Trade Classification -- SITC 5-8) between 2004 and 2006, also taking into account third market competition. This index should not be confused with the effective exchange rate of the euro calculated by the ECB on the basis of total euro area external trade. A positive (negative) value suggests appreciation (depreciation). Index 2000=100, period averages and percentage changes over previous period.

notes_excerpt: DESCRIPTION: Bulletin of conjunctural indicatorsNOTES: The real effective exchange rate (REER) is the nominal effective exchange rate deflated by a weighted geometric mean of appropriate relative price or cost indices. The REER indices compiled by the Bank of Greece include Greece's 28 major trading partners within and outside the euro area (broad index) and euro area countries (narrow index) and are CPI-deflated or HICP-deflated, where applicable. Weights are calculated on the basis of Greece's imports and exports of manufacturing goods (categories 5-8 of the Standard International Trade Classification -- SITC 5-8) between 2004 and 2006, also taking into account third market competition. A positive (negative) change in the indices suggests losses (gains) in Greece's competitiveness relative to its trading partners. Index 2000=100, period averages and percentage changes over previous period.The index is subject to regular revisions.
